summary: Herbert Mills Birdwood studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1851–1854) and Peterhouse (~1854–1858). He served in the Indian Civil Service from around 1858 to 1897.

Herbert Niel Randle studied at Dulwich College, Hertford College, Oxford, and the University of Oxford (D.Phil.). A scholar of Indology and philosophy, he was Professor of Philosophy at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Allahabad, later serving as Librarian at the India Office.

Herbert Petersson was a linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Lund University under Nils Olof Mathias Flensburg, also studying at Rostock, Münster, and Copenhagen. At Lund, he served as Docent (1911) and later ordinary Professor from 1923 to 1927.

Linguist and Indologist Herbert Pierrepont Houghton earned degrees from Amherst College and Johns Hopkins University, also studying at Princeton. He served as President of Waynesburg University (1908–1915) and later as Professor of Classics at Carleton College (1923–1950).
Philosopher Herbert Schneider studied at the City University of New York (~1911–1915) and Columbia University (~1915–1917). He held a post at Columbia University from around 1918 to 1957.
Indologist Herbert Tower Sorley studied at the University of Aberdeen (~1910–1914), earning an M.A., and later obtained a D.Litt. from the University of Sindh.

Herbert V. Guenther studied at Munich under Wilhelm Geiger and Vienna under Erich Frauwallner. Active in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, he taught at Lucknow and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University before heading the Far Eastern Studies department at Saskatchewan (1964–1984).

Herbert W. Duda worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held academic posts at the University of Leipzig (~1928–1932), the University of Breslau (~1932–1941), and the University of Vienna (~1943–1970).

Linguist and historian Herbert Weir Smyth studied at Swarthmore, Harvard, Leipzig, and Göttingen. He taught at Williams College, Johns Hopkins, and Bryn Mawr before serving as Eliot Professor of Greek Literature at Harvard from 1902 to 1925.

Herbert William Magoun studied at Grinnell College and Johns Hopkins University under Maurice Bloomfield. A scholar of Indology and linguistics, he held professorships at Oberlin and Redfield colleges, later serving as President of the Massachusetts College of Osteopathy (1921–1926).
Japanologist Herbert Zachert studied under Karl Florenz between ~1928 and 1933. He held posts at the Humboldt University of Berlin (~1949–1960) and the University of Bonn (~1960–1976).

Herman Almkvist studied at Uppsala, Paris, Leipzig (under Fleischer and Brockhaus), and the Collège de France. In linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies, he became extraordinary Professor of comparative linguistics (1878) and Professor of Semitic Languages (1892) at Uppsala.
Indologist Herman Eildert Buiskool studied under Barend Faddegon at the University of Amsterdam, earning his PhD in 1934. He served as a conservator at Leiden University from 1936 to 1938.
Indologist Herman Frederik Eelsingh completed his Ph.D. at Utrecht University in 1908 under the supervision of Willem Caland.

Linguist and Indologist Herman Kellgren studied at Helsinki, Berlin, Paris, Leipzig, and St. Petersburg under mentors including Bopp, Burnouf, and Fleischer. In 1854, he became Docent of Sanskrit at the University of Helsinki.
Herman Neubronner van der Tuuk worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Groningen from ~1840 to 1845 and at Leiden University from ~1845 to 1849.

Linguist Hermann Ammann studied under Rudolf Thurneysen at the University of Freiburg and at Heidelberg. He worked at the Thesaurus Linguae Latinae, taught at Freiburg, and became ordinary Professor of Indo-European and general linguistics at Innsbruck in 1928.

Hermann Beckh studied at Kiel and Humboldt University of Berlin under Richard Pischel and Georg Huth. Working in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, he was a PD at Berlin (1910–1921) and later taught at the Priesterseminar der Christengemeinschaft Stuttgart (~1922–1937).

Indologist and linguist Hermann Berger completed his doctorate at Munich under Helmut Hoffmann and Ferdinand Sommer. He served as a PD at Munich, visiting professor at Sanskrit College and University, and Director at Heidelberg University (1964–1993).

Hermann Beythan studied at the Leipzig Evangelical Lutheran Mission (1895–1901) and under traditional teachers Ramasami Aiyar and Raja Pillai. Working in Indology and linguistics, he was Lecturer in Tamil at the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen (1933–1945).
